headline: Deep learning models predict gene, drug and variant effects from biological priors
label: Knowledge Guided Biomedical Deep Learning
summary: Large perturbation, reporter and drug-response datasets now allow models that encode prior biological knowledge to predict unseen conditions.
synthesis: The shared thread is the incorporation of prior biological structure into deep models so they can predict responses to conditions absent from training. PerturbGraph combines PPI networks and GO features in a GNN to predict transcriptional responses to unseen gene perturbations from single-cell CRISPR data. PHENOCAUZ links human symptoms and drug side effects to proteins using Mendelian gene-phenotype data and machine learning. ME-NET adds pathway information to PBMC transcriptome models for multi-disease risk stratification and drug target discovery. DEPICT, a transformer, predicts condition-matched drug transcriptional responses on LINCS L1000 and generalizes to unseen drugs and cells. What is new across these items is the explicit use of prior knowledge to support generalization, with ME-NET adding interpretability. BlueSTARR and GP-WAITER extend the theme to noncoding regulatory variants and crop complex-trait prediction, using whole-genome STARR-seq and GWAS-derived SNP embeddings respectively.
